exceptions.reason: Spec 8.3's Noto Emoji substitution. U+1F600 and U+1F389 are absent from every official font chunk, so revision 1 shapes each from the complete monochrome Noto Emoji 3.003 face and reports one font.noto-emoji-substituted per affected occurrence (decided on #121). The official export has no bundled glyph for them either: its font list ends in the local-only Segoe UI Emoji, which the pinned container's fontconfig resolves to Noto Color Emoji 2.047, so the browser draws colour bitmap glyphs. The divergence is the emoji cells on both lines, colour bitmaps against monochrome outlines at near-identical advances, plus the trailing Latin word each cell shifts by at most three pixels. The leading Latin word on both lines differs only by the sub-pixel glyph-coverage class recorded on #104, #105, #108 and #110. With #169 the renderer snaps each line's baseline to the device pixel grid as the canvas does, so what remains is the two rasterizers' coverage of identically placed outlines.

purpose: Substitute emoji with the bundled Noto Emoji face as spec 8.3 requires: an Excalifont element carrying U+1F600 and U+1F389 and a Liberation Sans (fontFamily 9) element carrying U+1F600 each mix Latin with emoji no official chunk maps. The official export's font list ends in the local-only Segoe UI Emoji and draws whatever the browser's system-font fallback supplies for it; revision 1 shapes every emoji from the complete monochrome Noto Emoji 3.003 face, so the primary face and the replacement face both fall through to it, and reports one font.noto-emoji-substituted info per affected text occurrence rather than per scalar. No scalar belongs to the CJK table, so Xiaolai stays out of the fallback chain.
